dependencies.required_evidence: target-scale F archive gain, exact inverse, P/K synchronization, F/S causal control, deterministic repeat, and resource pass
probability-identical full roundtrip and strict memory qualification

contract.question: Is target-scale full-midpoint gain primarily local to bytes 32-63 or dependent on persistent parameter, optimizer, and recurrent-state changes?

arms.F: full persistent midpoint update from the qualified oracle
arms.J: run an untouched parent branch and an identical adapted branch from byte 32 through byte 63; code with the adapted branch; at byte 64 discard it and rejoin the untouched parent parameter, optimizer, recurrent, mixer, SSE, context, and memory state
arms.S: the oracle's frozen causally misaligned persistent midpoint update

J_branch_rules: Both branches consume the exact same already decoded truths.
Ordinary parent learning continues at original call sites in the untouched branch.
The adapted branch applies the same F update and ordinary cadence used by F.
The arithmetic coder consumes only J's selected adapted probabilities during the second half.
At byte 64 only model state rejoins; coder state and emitted payload continue normally.
No persistent write from the adapted branch may survive rejoin.

terminal_routes.J_below_0_8_and_functional_jvp_strong: authorize one persistent Tangent-MIDAS or Curvature-MIDAS realization selected by the JVP receipt

activation_requirements: selected execution host has no active exclusive_full1g lease
full midpoint oracle terminal pass is content-addressed
J's complete persistent write set and rejoin state hash are frozen
actual finite coder, exact decode, raw inverse, repeat, package, dependency, and resource receipts are bound
claim_boundary: The 0.80 branch is immutable after the first J archive.
